sources.citation: lexibank/chacontukanoan: CLDF dataset derived from Chacon 2014 'A revised proposal of Proto-Tukanoan consonants and Tukanoan family classification' (IJAL 80.3).
sources.note: lists Kueretu (ID KUE, glottocode cure1236) among 16 varieties; lexical/cognate data only, no prosodic annotation.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II: Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Coretú' pp. 164-166.
sources.note: Bare Latin-Coretú wordlist (footnote: taken by Martius from chief Pachicúh at S. João do Príncipe on the Japurá); diacritics present but no remarks on accent. The separate 'Curetú' list p. 284f (after Wallace) is Yupúa, with Martius's own footnote doubting its identity.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2019 [1997]. A Fala Tukano dos Ye'pâ-Masa, Tomo I: Gramática. Versão atualizada. Manaus: Inspetoria Salesiana Missionária da Amazônia / CEDEM. 309 pp. (Introduction pp. 4-12 on the Tukano family incl. †kueretú.)
sources.note: Only segmental/lexical history for Kueretú: lexical-distance table, tanimuka-†kueretú possible subgroup (*d > r before i, *b > h lenition 'recente e dialetal em †kueretú', *p > h), '*s tornou-se t [t̪] antes de V+post.. e s antes de V-post', heavy †mepuri (Arawak) loans. The accent/tone sections (pp. 37-65, 267ff) concern Ye'pâ-masa Tukano only. Nothing on Kueretú accent.
sources.venue: A Fala Tukano dos Ye'pâ-Masa, Tomo I: Gramática

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa. 2017. Supplementary Material Accompanying the Paper 'A Revised Proposal of Proto-Tukanoan Consonants and Tukanoan Family Classification' (IJAL 80.3, 2014). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.883632 (Edictor-aligned cognate dataset, CC-BY-4.0).
sources.note: Segmental IPA tokens and alignments only (e.g. KUE haja 'snake', kome 'nose', hijai 'jaguar'); no stress or tone marking, no notes. Wordlist-only data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa & Johann-Mattis List. 2015. Improved computational models of sound change shed light on the history of the Tukanoan languages. Journal of Language Relationship 13(3): 177-204.
sources.note: Kueretu (Kue) included as a Western Tukanoan variety from Koch-Grünberg's data; discusses consonant changes (*dz > j, *ts > t, t > n /~V_V in Kueretu); nothing on stress or accent in Kueretu.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1914. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete (Fortsetzung): Desána, Yupúa, Yahúna, Kueretú. Anthropos 9: 812-832.
sources.note: Four-column comparative wordlist; Kueretú forms carry an acute accent per item on varying syllables (p. 812: siámelako 'Zunge', sikoméo 'Nase', siakókia 'Auge', sikiatílo 'Ohr', stróho 'Kopf', strohóre 'Kopfhaar', sikiakómeno 'Schulter', simahúmpu 'Hand'); footnotes concern Yahúna/Yupúa segments only; no statement about accent placement.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1913. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete [I]. Anthropos 8: 944-977.
sources.note: General 'Lautlehre' (p. 948) for all his Betoya vocabularies lists only the diacritic: 'á Wortakzent.' (acute = word accent, marked per item); 'Bemerkungen zu den einzelnen Sprachen' (p. 949) has no Kueretú entry; p. 947 says the Kueretú list was taken March-April 1905 on the lower Apaporís; p. 950 names Martius 1867 II:164ff as the only earlier Kueretú source and says Wallace's 'Curetu' is really Yupúa. No stress rule.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1911. Affinités du Miránya. Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s. 8: 117-152.
sources.note: Nothing. Rivet states (p. 117) 'En l'absence de données grammaticales, je m'appuierai exclusivement sur des comparaisons lexicologiques' and the body is a French-glossed comparative word table (Miránya vs Tupi-Guarani, Uitoto, Záparo, Arawak, Carib, Peba, Tikuna, Makú, Tukano, etc.) followed by match counts. Kueretú (T3) contributes a handful of cited forms with acute accent marks copied from Koch-Grünberg; there is no remark on accent, stress, tone, syllables or pronunciation for Kueretú or any Tukano language. a full-text search for stress/accent the whole article span for accent/tonique/to…
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes n.s

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1910. Zwei Jahre unter den Indianern: Reisen in Nordwest-Brasilien 1903/1905, Bd. II (Kueretú passage c. pp. 306-309; Anhang: Wörterlisten with Lautlehre and 'Bemerkungen zu den einzelnen Sprachen'). Berlin: Ernst Wasmuth.
sources.note: Ethnographic passage: Kueretú remnant on the Rio Caritáya, 'Ihre Sprache gehört als unreines Glied der Betóyagruppe an'. Appendix Lautlehre again only 'á = Wortakzent' (generic); per-language remarks cover Kobéua, Yahúna, Uitóto, Miránya, Makú -- no Kueretú entry; only morphological note 'im Kueretú: si- = mein' (possessive prefix on body-part terms). Nothing on accent placement.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1906. Die Indianerstämme am oberen Rio Negro und Yapurá und ihre sprachliche Zugehörigkeit. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 38: 166-205.
sources.note: Transcription key for all his vocabularies (p. 190f): 'á = Wortakzent', 'ă = betonte Kürze'; per-language remarks (p. 191-192) have no Kueretú entry except that x is 'bisweilen gleich einem stark gutturalen h (h im Kueretú und Uitóto)'; p. 186-187 locates the Kueretú and says 'das Kueretú gehört, wenn auch als unreines Glied, der Betoyagruppe an'; p. 201 a 15-word Kobéua/Kueretú comparative table with acute accents per item (siámelako 'Zunge'..). No rule or remark on where the accent falls.
